scenes.picture: Chidi smiling proudly in his room, wearing a super white agbada, holding a plate of dripping palm oil stew.
scenes.dialogue: See my life! Epp me look fresh for campus party tonight.
scenes.caption: Chidi ready to paint campus red, but red stew wan paint am first.

scenes.picture: Chidi tripping over his roommate's bag, stew flying through the air like a rocket towards his white agbada.
scenes.dialogue: Ah! Village people, wetin I do una?!
scenes.caption: Physics assignment: calculate velocity of palm oil landing on white lace.

scenes.picture: Chidi crying as the agbada is now stained red. He tries to wash it inside a small plastic bucket with cheap yellow soap.
scenes.dialogue: Make I run wash am sharp sharp before e dry.
scenes.caption: Washing white agbada with yellow soap is spiritual warfare.

scenes.picture: Chidi holding up the agbada, now looking pink and shredded. The collar has completely torn off.
scenes.dialogue: Jesus! The cloth don turn pink tie-and-dye. Aunty Ngozi go kill me!
scenes.caption: From Agbada to Agbakwuru in two minutes.

scenes.picture: Aunty Ngozi standing at the doorway with hands on her waist, looking furious at the torn pink mess.
scenes.dialogue: Chidi! Where is the expensive agbada I gave you to dry-clean?!
scenes.caption: Aunty Ngozi don enter full Nollywood wicked landlady mode.

scenes.picture: Neat Naija attendant smiling, handing a brand new, neatly ironed sparkling white agbada to Chidi while Aunty Ngozi smiles in shock.
scenes.dialogue: No shaking, bro. Neat Naija don sort am!
scenes.caption: Laundry, house, office, sofa and carpet cleaning. DM to book.
